_comment: The Counsel's register. 'status' is the last confirmed status known to the model when written (2026-11-05) unless 'verified' says otherwise; rule 3 applies: a legal claim needs the primary text. Each entry carries the primary URL to read. 'applies_to' uses facility ids and regions so the Risk check can map regimes to a profile.

regimes.name: NERC CIP Reliability Standards (CIP-002 to CIP-015)
regimes.jurisdiction: US and Canada bulk electric system
regimes.status: in force; versions change; CIP-015 (internal network security monitoring) approved by FERC in 2025 with phased effective dates; the enforceable version of each standard must be checked on nerc.com
regimes.verified: model knowledge, unverified by this system
regimes.energy_impact: the mandatory cyber baseline for the grid; patching (CIP-007), change management (CIP-010), remote access (CIP-005), monitoring (CIP-015) are the clauses this week's Siemens, Zyxel and Ivanti items land on
regimes.intel_impact: CIP-008 incident reporting to E-ISAC feeds the sector's shared intelligence

regimes.name: FERC Order 887 (internal network security monitoring) and supply-chain orders
regimes.status: Order 887 (2023) directed NERC to develop INSM requirements; resulting standard CIP-015
regimes.energy_impact: makes protocol-aware monitoring inside control networks a requirement, the control the Industroyer and MicroSCADA cases argue for
regimes.intel_impact: more internal telemetry means more detection data to share

regimes.name: TSA Pipeline Security Directives (SD Pipeline-2021-01 and 02 series) and the proposed surface cyber rule
regimes.jurisdiction: US pipelines and LNG facilities designated by TSA
regimes.status: directives in force and reissued periodically; a notice of proposed rulemaking (Enhancing Surface Cyber Risk Management, 2024) would codify them; final rule status unverified; the paste says one secondary source lists SD Pipeline-2021-02F expiring 2 May 2026, so a reissued version probably exists
regimes.verified: model knowledge plus the project's own notes, unverified
regimes.energy_impact: post-Colonial regime: segmentation, access control, monitoring, incident reporting to CISA within 24 hours, assessment plans
regimes.intel_impact: mandatory reporting is a collection source for CISA; the directive's indicator-sharing clauses depend on CISA 2015 protections

regimes.name: Cybersecurity Information Sharing Act of 2015 (sunset)
regimes.status: liability protections for sharing threat indicators; sunset extended into late 2026 per the project's notes; Utility Dive reports expiry 'next month' (December 2026) and utilities urging renewal; NDAA extension pending [unverified]
regimes.verified: trade press only (Utility Dive 2026-11-04); statute text not read
regimes.energy_impact: if it lapses, lawyers advise less sharing; detection across the sector slows
regimes.intel_impact: the legal basis of E-ISAC and CISA indicator exchange; the single biggest cyber-intelligence policy item this week

regimes.name: CIRCIA (Cyber Incident Reporting for Critical Infrastructure Act) reporting rule
regimes.status: law 2022; CISA's final reporting rule (72-hour incident, 24-hour ransom payment) expected 2025-2026; final status unverified
regimes.energy_impact: mandatory incident reporting for covered energy entities once final
regimes.intel_impact: would give CISA a near-real-time picture of energy incidents, the dataset this society lacks

regimes.name: SEC cybersecurity disclosure rule (Form 8-K Item 1.05, Regulation S-K Item 106)
regimes.status: in force since December 2023: material incidents disclosed within four business days of materiality determination
regimes.energy_impact: Halliburton 2024 and similar disclosures come from this rule
regimes.intel_impact: 8-K filings are a primary-source stream the Economist and Archivist read

regimes.name: NRC 10 CFR 73.54 (cyber security for nuclear power reactors)
regimes.energy_impact: separation of safety and security systems; the reason Kudankulam-style IT infections do not reach control
regimes.intel_impact: reporting to NRC, not CISA; a separate channel

regimes.name: US Coast Guard maritime cybersecurity rule (MTSA facilities and vessels)
regimes.status: final rule published January 2025, effective July 2025, phased requirements
regimes.energy_impact: LNG terminals and tankers get cyber plans, training, incident reporting
regimes.intel_impact: reports flow to the Coast Guard and CISA

regimes.name: Executive order restricting foreign grid components (2026)
regimes.status: reported 2026-11-03: an order restricting foreign-sourced grid components; industry says geography-based restrictions miss function and capability and threaten investment; instrument and effective date not read [unverified]; lineage: EO 13920 (2020) on bulk-power-system equipment
regimes.verified: trade press only (Utility Dive); Federal Register text not read
regimes.energy_impact: changes who may supply transformers, inverters, controls; lead times and cost; the PIT layer's provenance
regimes.intel_impact: supply-chain security by policy; makes component provenance a reportable fact

regimes.name: EU NIS2 Directive (2022/2555)
regimes.status: in force; transposition deadline October 2024, uneven across states; energy is a 'highly critical' sector; 24-hour early warning, 72-hour notification
regimes.energy_impact: management liability, supply-chain duties, incident reporting for energy entities including small ones
regimes.intel_impact: national CSIRTs receive early warnings; the French blood-service and supermarket cases fall under its reporting regime

regimes.name: EU Network Code on Cybersecurity for the electricity sector (Regulation 2024/1366)
regimes.energy_impact: risk assessments and minimum controls for cross-border electricity flows; interconnectors
regimes.intel_impact: creates an EU-level cyber risk picture for electricity

regimes.name: EU Cyber Resilience Act (Regulation 2024/2847)
regimes.jurisdiction: products with digital elements sold in the EU
regimes.status: in force December 2024; vulnerability-reporting obligations from September 2026; main obligations December 2027
regimes.energy_impact: inverters, routers, controllers sold in the EU must ship with secure defaults and vulnerability handling; the Zyxel, Welotec and Siemens items are the product class
regimes.intel_impact: manufacturers must report actively exploited vulnerabilities to ENISA within 24 hours, a new intelligence stream

regimes.name: UK Cyber Security and Resilience Bill and NIS Regulations 2018
regimes.status: NIS Regulations in force; the Bill introduced 2025 to widen scope and reporting; passage status unverified
regimes.energy_impact: broader coverage of suppliers and data centres
regimes.intel_impact: NCSC's annual review (this week) is the policy signal behind it

regimes.name: Australia SOCI Act and Critical Infrastructure Risk Management Program rules
regimes.status: in force; updated CIRMP guidance published, urging stronger cyber and supply-chain controls (Industrial Cyber, 2026-11-04)
regimes.verified: trade press for the update; statute from model knowledge
regimes.energy_impact: risk management programmes with supply-chain duties for energy operators
regimes.intel_impact: CISC guidance is a primary source the allowlist cannot fetch directly (ACSC feed unreachable)

regimes.name: Canada Bill C-8 (Critical Cyber Systems Protection Act, successor to C-26)
regimes.jurisdiction: Canada federally regulated sectors including energy
regimes.regulator: Canadian Centre for Cyber Security; regulators
regimes.energy_impact: mandatory programmes and reporting for pipelines and interprovincial power; Nova Scotia Power 2025 is the reference case

regimes.name: Japan Active Cyber Defense law (2025)
regimes.energy_impact: critical-infrastructure operators report incidents; government may act against attacking infrastructure
regimes.intel_impact: a state intelligence posture change in Asia; JPCERT is now in the allowlist

news_this_week.headline: US midterm elections: Democrats take control of both the House and the Senate (per MIT Technology Review); a lame-duck session precedes the change
news_this_week.what: CyberScoop reports the incoming leaders of the homeland security panels are setting cyber agendas, with CISA and AI among the priorities named in its URL; MIT Technology Review asks what changes in US energy policy.
news_this_week.energy_impact: [inference] the direction of federal energy policy (permitting, grid investment, data-centre load, foreign-component rules) changes with the majority; the specifics are not in the summaries and the Counsel has not read the agendas.
news_this_week.intel_impact: [inference] CISA's funding, authorities and leadership direction, and whether the CISA 2015 sunset is fixed in the lame-duck session, are the two levers for cyber intelligence; both are decided in the next weeks.
news_this_week.confidence: moderate on the fact of the result (two outlets); low on implications

news_this_week.headline: Cybersecurity Information Sharing Act of 2015 expiring next month; electric utilities join industries urging renewal
news_this_week.what: Liability protection for sharing threat indicators among companies and with federal agencies is weeks from sunset; renewal is being lobbied.
news_this_week.energy_impact: Utilities share less if counsel sees liability; E-ISAC and CISA exchange thins.
news_this_week.intel_impact: This society's own collection depends on operators disclosing; a lapse makes the US 'quiet week' structurally quieter. The single most important item on the register this week.

news_this_week.headline: Executive order restricting foreign grid components; industry objects to geography-based restrictions
news_this_week.what: Stakeholders applauded the intent but said restrictions by country of origin rather than by function and capability miss the point and threaten investment.
news_this_week.energy_impact: Transformer and inverter sourcing, lead times and cost; the PIT layer of substations and renewables.
news_this_week.intel_impact: Makes component provenance a security fact to track; shifts the supply-chain map in the Research tab.

news_this_week.headline: Texas data-centre buildout may stall after the state's election results (MIT Technology Review)
news_this_week.what: Texas is the fastest-growing US data-centre market; the article argues the state's election results may jeopardise that position.
news_this_week.energy_impact: [inference] data-centre siting decides where gigawatts of new load and the cooling OT that comes with it appear; a shift away from Texas moves grid stress elsewhere.
news_this_week.intel_impact: [inference] the Technologist's beat: load as a security variable; where compute goes, the attack surface follows.

news_this_week.headline: Australia's CISC publishes updated Critical Infrastructure Risk Management Program guidance
news_this_week.what: Updated guidance urging stronger cyber and supply-chain controls under the SOCI Act.
news_this_week.energy_impact: Australian energy operators tighten supply-chain duties.
news_this_week.intel_impact: Another regulator naming supply chain as the control; convergent with the US order and the EU CRA.

news_this_week.headline: White House-backed Project Lifeline 250: secure remote access for rural hospitals (Dispel joins)
news_this_week.what: A federal programme with vendors to secure OT remote access at rural hospitals.
news_this_week.energy_impact: [inference] the same remote-access problem at rural cooperatives has no equivalent programme yet; a model to copy.

news_this_week.headline: UK NCSC Annual Review: AI-assisted ransomware against critical national infrastructure by 2028
news_this_week.what: Agency forecast and investment case; the policy signal behind the UK Cyber Security and Resilience Bill.
news_this_week.energy_impact: CNI operators told to fund basics.
news_this_week.intel_impact: Names China as best positioned; a primary-source assessment of capability.

counsel_note: I have read none of the instruments above this run; every status line is the last confirmed status with its date, and the Risk check shows regimes as 'applies, unverified'. Primary URLs are attached so a person or the next scheduled run can read them. Rule 3.
